Theorem
[Conjugate Point Comparison I]

↗ thm:jacobi-field-comparison

1. ch11:11.12

Let $(M,g)$ be a Riemannian manifold with $\sec _M\leq c$. If $c\leq 0$, no point has a conjugate point along any geodesic. If $c=1/R^2>0$, no geodesic segment of length less than $\pi R$ contains conjugate endpoints.

Proof

\sketch Let $J$ be a nonzero normal Jacobi field along a unit-speed geodesic, with $J(0)=0$. Then $D_tJ(0)\ne 0$. If $c\leq 0$, comparison with $c=0$ gives

\[ |J(t)|\geq t|D_tJ(0)|>0 \]

for $t>0$. If $c=1/R^2>0$, Jacobi comparison gives

\[ |J(t)|\geq R\sin (t/R)|D_tJ(0)|>0 \]

for $0<t<\pi R$. Thus $J$ cannot vanish again in the stated ranges.

□
